name: Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Sur

profile.campus: Banco Santander CPD Cantabria (Norte/Sur), Medio Cudeyo, Cantabria
profile.reading: This is the Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Sur, the south building of Banco Santanders main Spanish data processing campus in the Medio Cudeyo area near Solares, Cantabria, in northern Spain, paired with a companion Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Norte building on the same site. Banco Santander inaugurated the Cantabria data center on December 16, 2011, describing it at the time as the banks fifth data center worldwide, joining existing facilities in Madrid, London, Queretaro in Mexico, and Campinas in Brazil, and stated the new center increased the banks overall data processing capacity by 30 percent. Direct construction investment exceeded 240 million euros, with an additional 104 million euros in public and private investment supporting the surrounding industrial area, and the site sits on a roughly 300,000 square meter parcel offering room for future expansion, with the built facility described at the time as spanning over 6,000 square meters. The center has since been referred to locally as El Bunker for its security profile, housing the banks Centro de Control de Sistemas. In February 2022, local press reported that IT services contractor Indra Soluciones dismissed about 35 percent of its Cantabria data center workforce, following an earlier 2021 decision by Santander Global Tech to relocate roles previously performed in Cantabria to Madrid, a move regional union representatives disputed given that much of the remaining workforce already operated remotely with positive performance reviews. Banco Santander was founded in 1857 as Banco de Santander in the city of Santander, Cantabria, which remains its legal headquarters even as day to day operations are run from Boadilla del Monte near Madrid. The bank reported total assets of about 1.84 trillion dollars as of the third quarter of 2025, ranked as the 16th largest banking institution in the world and Europes 4th largest bank by assets per an April 2026 S&P Global report, with roughly 206,753 employees across Europe, South America, North America, and Asia as of 2024, underscoring the operational weight the Cantabria data processing campus carries for a bank of global scale headquartered in the same region.
